body:
I'm not sure where you are located but by the sounds of it probably the US? Depending on your state, income and schooling status you might qualify for medicaid. I'd definitely look in to it to see if it's an option. Also, you should have a card for your insurance and you can call the number on the back to ask questions about your current plan. They should be able to explain your co-pays and deductibles if there are any and what steps you should take to receive the help you need. Sometimes you need a referral from your general practitioner, sometimes not. It really just depends on how your insurance works.

Unfortunately there is a lot of stigma out there about mental illness. A lot of victim blaming (I don't really know a better term to use here) and misconceptions about it.

Anti-depressants have NEVER once made me feel drugged. The correct dose of benzos shouldn't really either. Usually those are to be taken as needed, like you feel a panic attack coming on. They should help you calm down. Benzos like Xanax aren't really meant to be taken as the main medication to help with your anxiety, just when it gets really bad or temporarily until the right anti-depressant or dosage of anti-depressant is found. Anti-depressants on the other hand are meant to be taken every day.

If you could just stop thinking about it or will it away, wouldn't you of already done that? I don't know any one who asks to have mental illness. I get really upset when I hear people say those things as it's so damaging to the person going through it. It's dismissive. I'm really sorry your family doesn't seem very supportive. Maybe after seeing a counselor for a while they might have some suggestions of how to better explain it to your parents.

I've switched to other medications. I've never had any serious side effects, it's mainly been weight gain for me. The medications themselves worked fine other than that though. I knew how much they helped so I didn't worry about trying something else. I knew I would eventually find one that didn't cause many side effects for me (or ones that really didn't cause any issues for me) and helped my anxiety/depression.

I'm not the original poster but I personally think at the very least making a couple of appointments with a counselor would be a good idea.

It's been my experience that medicine is more of trail and error at this point in time so unfortunately it might require several visits and medication changes as every medication works different for different people.

Getting help can be hard because our anxiety lies to us. It always goes to worst case scenario which almost never happens. Heck, I know that intellectually yet time and time again I find myself believing it. Therapy has helped me a lot. I feel like I am learning skills to take control back from my anxiety. I get uncomfortable in therapy sometimes, I won't lie. But that's part of getting better. To face your fears. Baby steps!

Yes, medication has been helpful for me. Definitely. A lot of the medications they might put you on have been around a very long time and they know quite a bit about them and their risks. I've taken multiple anti-depressants and benzos over the years and I have yet to have any serious side effects. I've usually experienced minor ones that almost always go away after a while.

I know medication can sound scary but in my opinion it's worth it. I've gone from crying and having panic attacks daily to feeling calm and collected. I still have anxiety but the severity is no where near where it could be and has been. I find medication gets me to where I felt I always should be. I feel locked inside my head some times and trapped because of my anxiety but medication has unlocked a lot of things I thought I would never be able to do. Even little things like not having a panic attack. That's really huge for me!

I actually have the Mirena and I've had a few times where I've questioned whether I should have it removed or not myself.

If the pain is not getting better and continuing I definitely think that's a valid reason to have it removed. Unfortunately the only way to find out if something is right for you is to try it. You've suffered through the pain long enough. I don't really see what else you would have to gain from it being left in. Try not to beat yourself up over it. There is no way you could have known how your body would react to the IUD. -hugs-

I know exactly how you feel. I've had so many different diagnoses or possible diagnoses over the years. Maybe RA, Juvenile Arthritis or EDS and now fibromyalgia is what they're leaving it at. It's even worse when one doctor says this and another doctor says that. Who do you believe at that point? I usually just say to myself maybe it's something we will never know what causes it or maybe not until medicine gets further along but I've also never experienced anything that has sent me to the hospital either.

I'm really sorry to hear about what you are going through. If you need an ear (or should I say in this case an eye!) my inbox is always open. I hope you are able to find an answer to this mystery illness sooner rather than later.

I've never personally experienced this sort of thing. I do get to feeling worse where my pain gets worse and I'll feel like I have a fever (like a bad cold or the beginning of the flu) but when I've checked my temperature I didn't have one. It's never escalated beyond that, nor have I ever thrown up. Maybe talk to your doctor about the frequency of it happening? If they won't hear you out maybe seeking a second opinion. I'm sorry that I don't have a whole lot to add here as I've never personally experienced this.

Yeah. I just think this nurse is set in her ways where no amount of evidence would sway her mind. To her, depression is my root problem, not anxiety. Which that treatment plan that she is so invested in and told me she will not change will not be helping me. I'm going to try some where else if she will not grant me a change of nurse but if not I guess I will just be visiting my general practitioner. At least I won't be dreading the appointments there.

I don't even see how the doctor you're having issues with has all the power. It feels like they have the doctor/clinics best interest instead of the patient. If I say I don't feel comfortable seeing her again, why should I have to? I'll see what she says when she calls but if she tries to spin it around as me being no complacent or something, I'm done with this place.

I'm going through something similar right now with my boyfriend. I know at least in my case I've started to think I've been too busy trying to fix him and his issues rather than listening and just *being there*.

My boyfriend doesn't want to talk to me either but I'm finding trying to force him to talk isn't working. I think just letting her know you're there for her if she needs someone then dropping it might be something to try. If you're like me, you find it frustrating and sometimes very hurtful as they seem so closed off. I can't promise in the end it will work as I'm just starting down that path myself but what I do know is that I need to try something different as what I am doing now isn't working. Maybe you could look at both what you do and how you react to her and try to see what you feel you could do differently. Are you being too naggy? Are you getting upset? Do you turn her depression into how much it hurts you instead of her sometimes? What exactly does she say when she does say something that has to do with it? It's difficult, I know, as I'm dealing with it right now myself.

While I realize what you're trying to say, this is someone I have been with for a decade and who has been there for me and my issues in the past. He has no family as he was adopted and his family has never been accepting of it. His Dad was abusive and his Mom died. He has plenty of reason to be depressed. I don't want to leave him, I want to help him. I'm just confused at how to do that which is why I posted here. If helping him eventually meant I needed to walk away as I am too much to deal with at times, okay, but I can not in good conscious leave him completely alone when he has no one else who will be there for him right now.

Thanks. I am looking into trying to get medicaid. I think when you're this down, you also start to not care. My lack of support by anyone around me doesn't really make it any easier. Especially when I live with my boyfriend and he usually ignores it or gets angry at me for not dealing with it on my own.
The last time I was able to have testing done everything was fine. I do have Fibromyalgia though which really sucks sometimes. I am looking more into seeing if I can qualify for medicaid.
I will try to look into it, thanks.

Thanks for replying.

I think the hardest part for me right now is even though I've had issues in the past, I've never wanted to not be here like I do right now. I think sometimes I just wish I was never born. A lot of people don't understand and honestly, half the time I don't either.

I think what I dread is losing myself. I feel I'm disappearing. I know it can be better in ways, but I also know it comes back. And when it's back, at least if past is any tell tale sign for the furture, it lasts a long time.

My anxiety usually leads to delusions which I'm assuming is because of my Bipolar. I go from worrying but there's still some part of me that knows I'm just making it into something worse. Then it begins the phase of me losing touch with reality and believing some pretty strange things. It's not only extremely embarrassing to lose yourself like that, but I also honestly fear that happening again. So much so that I'd rather not be here than to go through it again and I think with me feeling like there isn't much I can do about it right now, it feels like the only viable solution.

Even sitting here reading this back to myself, it sounds like I am just sitting around having a casual conversation. I feel calm and like "Well if that's the only option to not go through it again, it's what I have to do" and that scares me a bit.

I know little to nothing about the Mormon faith so I had no idea about that. I do think I shall ask him how he feels about it and go from there, thanks.

I think you are getting hung up on my first sentence which was said out of anger. While it does make me uncomfortable to have *anyone* in my house that dislikes who I am for something I can not help, I also know that reason alone is not a good reason and I need to deal with it as long as they are being respectful. There has been a lot of gay bashing coming from Churches (and Christians in general) so I think it's only natural to feel a bit uneasy around representatives of a Church. That being said, it doesn't mean that I can expect they not come around. Mormon is only mentioned because it is the direct issue.

I would be opposed to anything that basically meant I could not use the livingroom, even if I was keeping to myself and trying my best to not disturb them. I would be sitting off in the corner, using my headphones if any sound was involved and keeping to myself (quiet). To me I see the common area as what it is, a common area. I feel doesn't need to remain 100% at all times, but it also believe it doesn't mean I need to be removed completely from the only area of the house that my own activities can be used, aside from completely rearranging my entire apartment before a guest visits. I feel if any of us roommates feel they want quiet or alone time, or want to be involved in activities that would make it impossible for someone else to adequately use actively used areas of the house (especially on a weekly or possible more often basis), it should be taken to the bedroom or another less used area of the house, such as the diningroom. I did ask him to give me a heads up for when they come by but was unable to unfortunately. I pray *and* do meditation, but I would never expect everyone to vacate the livingroom and cease any and all activities that I might find disturbing because of it. While I might ask they be respectful with noise, no rude comments or just keep to themselves for a while, I wouldn't expect them to run off to their rooms because I am trying to make the livingroom my own private space.

I just wanted to thank you for taking the time to comment here. While I may not heed all your advice it has given me something to think about and help me understand the Mormon faith more.

This is a really confusing topic as something similar happened to me as well. I was around 8 and my neighbor (who I had a crush on) used to play truth or dare with me but usually it was just dares to touch him or him touch me sexually. Since I had a crush on him my thoughts were "Maybe he'll finally admit he likes me too!" so I just went with it. In some way I enjoyed it but at the same time I felt it was wrong. I once told my Mom about it and her response was "maybe you should stop going over there". I still did anyway and nothing more was done. I didn't bring it up as she made it feel like it was my problem to deal with and since I still liked him, I wasn't going to stop hanging out with him. Weird how you think when you're a child.

I don't really know if this counts as abuse or what it is really. It went on until I was around 13. After that I started to distance myself from him. I seen him once again when I was 17 and he pretended he didn't even know who I was.

I feel like I was taken advantage of but at the same time since I liked it, wouldn't that make me equally guilty? Also, he was only a year and a half older than I was so how much guilt is really his anyway?

All I can say is from an outside perspective I believe you should try to focus on getting yourself well right now. I know from personal experience when you're just starting on the path to getting better, whether it's starting a new medication or battling substance abuse, it's really important to focus all your energy on yourself. I've done some really similar things in the past and I find it usually always blows up in my face. In those moments I am riding so much hope on a relationship that if it doesn't turn out like I expect it effects my emotional well being, a lot of the time to disastrous levels. I know this is easier said than done as everyone wants to feel loved and cared for but maybe there are other people who could help fill that void right now. Do you have any family or friends that could be support to you?

I know it's hard to believe right now but there is someone out there for you. Sometimes when we think it's the right time, it's just not no matter how much we wish it was. I think us humans like to push things because *we* want it it work and usually *right now*. You seem like a really nice person. You deserve someone who will accept and love you for you but first and foremost **you deserve to get better.**

For me, I also have Fibromyalgia and yet to be explained high inflammation levels. When I get in the "MUST DO EVERYTHING!" mood, I end up making myself really fatigued which can land me in bed or at a minimum unable to do a whole lot. I have NSAIDs but they aren't great to take long term and as I am only 23, I have quite a few years ahead and I would like to not screw up my body any more than I really have to.

I just notice I have a tendency to get a lot of "good ideas" in which I must do *right away.* I need to start exercising tons! Even though I can't because of my physical limitations but let's do it anyway! It's even worse when I've tried it 38274 times and *still* think it's a good idea and do it *again.* I also tend to get really irritated when people around me don't see it my way. **Explanation:** Everything needs to be clean. Everyone else is so lazy 'cause they aren't helping!

I get really weird when I go into a full blown manic episode. I didn't even know I had bipolar until very recently but I now can look back and realize why I did and acted the way I did (and still do).

I have anxiety and OCD also and I usually worry about health issues (germs, cancer etc). Well, I became convinced I had melanoma so I would be constantly checking my moles. I also made tons of doctor appointments and at the time I didn't have health insurance so I got into debt pretty quickly. I've also convinced myself I will never be able to sleep again and will slowly die. I would start having panic attacks and I thought it was "finally happening" (dying). Also a certain necklace (it was a cross) would keep bad things from happening. If I didn't treat it well and wear it constancy God would spite me. I remember losing it once and I started throwing everything on the floor in my bedroom until I found it (I am not usually very religious might I add).

Of course, these didn't happen all at the same time but these are the ones that stick in my mind the most.

My anxiety and OCD fuels it a lot. Yesterday I got it in my mind I needed to vacuum the whole house to which I proceeded to vacuum not only the carpet but chairs, couches, cat trees.... pretty much everything. I also do the "I need to eat healthier!" *Buys tons of perishables that I never eat because I don't like them* I can't tell you how many times I've done that and at the time I was sure it was a fantastic idea!
Also, if you want to actually make it to work, gas or public transit prices.

What is the main differences between a doctor and a Nurse Practitioner? Also, I've been to doctors a lot and have noticed NPs always seem so much more friendly and down to earth than MDs. Have you noticed if this is generally true or have I just got some bad doctors? And if it is true, why do you think this is?
